Marathon Petroleum gained 1.46% today, continuing a modest upward trend over the past two weeks (+3.77%). The stock's strength reflects tightening conditions in global oil markets: U.S. refineries are running at 97.4% capacity—near maximum operational levels—while a U.S. Navy blockade of Iran has sharply reduced Iranian oil exports. With crude prices holding firm (U.S. oil at $83.90/barrel), refiners like Marathon benefit from sustained demand and constrained supply that supports margins.

The broader backdrop is a shift toward economic pressure on Iran rather than military action, which stabilizes the geopolitical risk premium in energy prices. This removes some of the volatility that characterized earlier in the month, allowing the refining sector to operate at high utilization without the shock risk that had weighed on sentiment before late August.
